metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Wisconsin (2026): Rules & Exemptions

description: Wisconsin has a statewide sales tax, but qualifying bullion (coins, bars, rounds, sheets) is fully exempt if it contains at least 35% precious metal.

What's covered by the exemption
Coins, bars, rounds, and sheets containing at least 35% precious metal.
How they decide what counts as bullion
The product must contain at least 35% precious metal and be in a typical bullion form (coin, bar, round, or sheet).
What's NOT covered
Collector coins below the 35% precious-metal threshold, jewelry, and accessories.
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Wisconsin.
Is gold and silver bullion taxable in Wisconsin?
+
No. Wisconsin fully exempts qualifying bullion products from sales tax when they meet the state’s bullion definition.
What bullion products are covered by Wisconsin’s exemption?
+
The exemption covers coins, bars, rounds, sheets, and similar bullion products that qualify under the state rule.
Does Wisconsin require a minimum precious-metal content for tax-free bullion?
+
Yes. Under the newer law, the product must be at least 35% precious metal to qualify as exempt bullion.
Are numismatic (collector) coins taxed in Wisconsin?
+
It depends. Numismatic items are treated conditionally and may be taxed if they fall outside Wisconsin’s bullion definition.
Is jewelry sales-tax exempt in Wisconsin?
+
No. Jewelry is taxable in Wisconsin even though qualifying bullion is exempt.
